source_references.description: Complete, revision-matched arXiv TeX source package

analysis.reason: The paper investigates gravitational waveform modeling and observational detectability for subsolar-mass NS-BH binaries formed via collapsar accretion disk fragmentation, which directly relates to supernova central engines and long gamma-ray burst progenitor environments.
analysis.result: Current LVK O4 subsolar searches suffer severe detection losses for collapsar-origin NS-BH binaries due to early tidal disruption and waveform dephasing, yielding an event detection fraction $\epsilon = ({\rm FF}\times B)^3 \sim 10^{-2}$ for light neutron stars ($m_{\rm NS} \simeq 0.1\,M_\odot$). Consequently, the actual merger rate upper limit $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon$ is weakened by several orders of magnitude compared to published point-mass bounds, matching the long gamma-ray burst rate $\mathcal{R}_0 \simeq 80\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ only near chirp mass $\mathcal{M}_c \simeq 2\,M_\odot$.
analysis.reading_entry: II Detection loss from individual phase corrections
analysis.problem: Standard stellar evolution cannot produce remnant black holes or core-collapse neutron stars below $M_{\mathrm{Ch}} \simeq 1.45\,M_\odot\,(Y_e/0.5)^2$, leaving the origin and observational detectability of potential subsolar-mass compact binaries in collapsar disks unconstrained by standard point-mass templates.
analysis.method: A frequency-domain TaylorF2 post-Newtonian model $\tilde{h}_{\texttt{NSBHc}}(f;\bm{\theta}) = \tilde{h}_{0}(f;\bm{\theta})\,\mathcal{S}_{*}(f;\bm{\theta})\,\mathcal{S}_{\text{end}}(f;\bm{\theta})\exp[{\rm i}\,\delta\psi(f;\bm{\theta})]$ is constructed, incorporating window functions and phase corrections $\delta\psi = \delta\psi_{\rm env}+\delta\psi_{\rm ecc}+\delta\psi_{\rm SIQM}+\delta\psi_{\rm tidal}$. Crucial dynamical corrections include Type I gas migration ($-4$PN) $\delta\psi_{\rm env} = -\frac{25C_{\rm I}}{2496\pi}\frac{f_{\rm disk}\dot{M}_{\rm BH}}{\alpha\mathbb{H}^4}v^{-8}\psi_{\rm N}$, residual eccentricity ($-19/6$PN), spin-induced quadrupole moments (2PN), and tidal deformability (5PN).
limits: Published LVK subsolar merger rate limits are weakened by orders of magnitude for light subsolar neutron stars, missing $\gtrsim 90\%$ of potential events.
citation_leads: 3400 North Charles Street, Baltimore, Maryland, 21218, USA: “Standard stellar evolution produces neither remnant black holes (BHs) nor ordinary core-collapse neutron stars”
3400 North Charles Street, Baltimore, Maryland, 21218, USA: “We model the GW signal from the collapsar NS-BH coalescence using the frequency-domain TaylorF2 PN template”
3400 North Charles Street, Baltimore, Maryland, 21218, USA: “the bound is weaker by orders of magnitude for light NSs, for which $\epsilon\sim 10^{-2}$”
I Template bank, pipelines, and black-hole spin: “For light NSs, all three pipelines miss $\gtrsim 90\%$ of the events.”
II Detection loss from individual phase corrections: “shifts in the template parameters depends primarily on its frequency dependence.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that detection loss in aligned-spin template banks depends critically on the frequency dependence of phase corrections: $-4$PN gas migration ($\\propto v^{-8}$) produces severe mismatch for light black holes, while 5PN tidal and 2PN spin-induced quadrupole effects are largely absorbed by template parameter redefinitions.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Left and middle columns: fraction of collapsar NS-BH events missed by the GstLAL O4 subsolar search, $1-{\rm FF}^{3}$ [Eq. ( 15 )], for $f_{\text{\tiny disk}}=0$ and $10^{-3}$. The black dashed line marks the LVK template-bank boundary at $q=0.1$, and the gray dotted line marks the curve $f_{\text{\tiny Roche}}=f_{\text{\tiny ISCO}}$ [Eq. ( 4 )], above which the NS reaches the ISCO before being disrupted. For $m_{\text{\tiny NS}}\lesssim 0.073\,M_{\odot}$, the NS is disrupted before the GW frequency reaches $f_{\text{\tiny min}}=45\,$ Hz. Right column: upper limit on the collapsar NS-BH merger rate, $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon$ [Eq. ( 17 )], from the GstLAL O4a+b limits $\mathcal{R}_{90}$ [ 4 ], with $\epsilon$ relative to template waveforms of the same chirp mass ($f_{\text{\tiny disk}}=0$). The top panel shows this limit in the $(M_{\text{\tiny BH}},m_{\text{\tiny NS}})$ plane. The red dashed contour marks $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon=\mathcal{R}_{0}$, where $\mathcal{R}_{0}$ is the LGRB rate, and the gray contour marks the boundary $\mathcal{M}_{c}=2.5\,M_{\odot}$ of the last LVK chirp-mass bin, beyond which no limit is available. The bottom panel shows $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon$ versus $\mathcal{M}_{c}$ for $M_{\text{\tiny BH}}=3\,M_{\odot}$ (blue) and $30\,M_{\odot}$ (green, dashed), with $m_{\text{\tiny NS}}$ from $\simeq 0.07$ to $1\,M_{\odot}$; the shaded band covers intermediate values of $M_{\text{\tiny BH}}$. Black squares mark $\mathcal{R}_{90}$ at the bin centers, and the red dashed line indicates $\mathcal{R}_{0}$.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Quantifies the fraction of collapsar subsolar NS-BH binary mergers missed by LVK O4 searches due to extreme mass ratios, tidal disruption prior to ISCO ($f_{\rm Roche} = f_{\rm ISCO}$), and accretion disk gas effects, establishing the astrophysically corrected merger rate upper limits $\mathcal{R}_{90}/\epsilon$ across the $(M_{\rm BH}, m_{\rm NS})$ parameter space and chirp mass $\mathcal{M}_c$ relative to the empirical long GRB rate $\mathcal{R}_0$.

figures.caption: Figure S4: Fraction of collapsar NS-BH events missed because of a single phase correction, $1-\mathcal{F}^{3}$ [Eq. ( S2 )], against aligned-spin TaylorF2 templates that end at the disruption of the signal, with $q\geq 10^{-4}$ and $|\chi_{1,2}|\leq 0.99$. Top: $f_{\text{\tiny min}}=45\,$ Hz; bottom: $f_{\text{\tiny min}}=20\,$ Hz, both up to $1024\,$ Hz. Columns, from left to right: migration with $f_{\text{\tiny disk}}=10^{-3}$ and $10^{-4}$, the tidal phase, and eccentricity $e_{\text{\tiny NS}-\text{\tiny BH}}=0.1$ at $f_{\text{\tiny min}}$. Gray: the NS is disrupted below $f_{\text{\tiny min}}$. Hatched: migration is faster than GW emission at $f_{\text{\tiny min}}$ [Eq. ( 11 )], and Eq. ( 10 ) does not apply. The SIQM term gives $1-\mathcal{F}^{3}\lesssim 3\times 10^{-2}$ in both bands and is not shown.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: Isolates and quantifies the physical mechanisms responsible for gravitational waveform dephasing and event loss, separating the effects of environmental disk migration torques ($f_{\rm disk}$), neutron star tidal deformation, and residual orbital eccentricity ($e_{\rm NS-BH}$) across the $(M_{\rm BH}, m_{\rm NS})$ plane.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a 17-year multi-wavelength analysis of 3C 454.3 showing that the long-term optical/gamma-ray correlation breaks down into epoch-dependent behavior on sub-day timescales, directly constraining relativistic jet emission mechanisms and multi-zone structures.
analysis.problem: Investigating whether the strong long-term optical/$\gamma$-ray correlation in blazar 3C 454.3 holds on intra-day timescales ($\le 24\,\mathrm{h}$) and testing canonical single-zone leptonic models (EC vs. SSC) against multi-zone or structured jet scenarios.
analysis.method: Combined 17-year Fermi-LAT and AGILE-GRID ($0.1-10\,\mathrm{GeV}$) observations with optical $R$-band photometry from WEBT; modeled $\gamma$-ray spectra with a log-parabola $\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}E}(E) = N_{0}\left(\frac{E}{E_{b}}\right)^{-\left[\alpha+\beta\ln\left(E/E_{b}\right)\right]}$ with $E_b = 908\,\mathrm{MeV}$, evaluated Spearman correlation coefficients $\rho_S$, fitted power-law scaling $L_{\gamma}\propto L_{R}^{\eta}$, and mapped the evolution of the Compton dominance $\mathrm{CD}$.
assumptions: The gamma-ray and optical luminosity scale as a power law $L_{\gamma} \propto L_{R}^{\eta}$ across stationary emitting intervals.
citation_leads: 2 3C 454.3: variability and optical-$gamma$-ray correlation: “variously attributing the high-energy emission to one-zone EC, SSC, mixed EC+SSC, or multi-zone EC scenarios.”
5 Global light curve properties: “Assuming $L_{\gamma}\propto L_{R}^{\eta}$, the best-fit slopes are $\eta=1.67\pm 0.02$”
6.4 Temporal structure of fast flares: “Such large $\mathrm{CD}$ variations on intra-day timescales challenge standard one-zone models”
8.1 A hierarchy of complexity: “the failure of standard one-zone models is not restricted to orphan flares or extreme states”
9 Conclusions: “statistical superposition of multiple physical regimes rather than a single radiative process.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that the global correlation with super-linear slope $\eta \approx 1.6-1.7$ represents a statistical superposition of distinct physical regimes rather than a single zone; rapid intra-day $\mathrm{CD}$ swings up to $\sim 120$ and fast variability timescales $t_{\mathrm{var}} \lesssim 3\,\mathrm{h}$ invalidate canonical homogeneous one-zone models, requiring localized dissipation sub-regions such as magnetic reconnection or BLR cloud fly-bys ($f_{\rm fly-by} \simeq 2-3$).

Red squares show the $48\text{\,}\mathrm{h}$ AGILE data during the AGILE-only period; blue circles the $24\text{\,}\mathrm{h}$ Fermi light curve; orange diamonds indicate the $30\text{\,}\mathrm{d}$ binned Fermi flux during the 2011-2013 quiescent period (MJD 55743-56293); arrows represent $95\%$ confidence level upper limits. Bottom panel: $R$ -band optical light curve. Grey vertical shaded areas mark the individual flaring epochs selected in Table 1.

figures.physical_core: Displays the 17-year (2007--2024) long-term multi-frequency light curves of 3C 454.3, combining $0.1-10\text{ GeV}$ $\gamma$-ray monitoring from AGILE ($48\text{ h}$) and Fermi-LAT ($24\text{ h}$ and $30\text{ d}$) with simultaneous WEBT optical $R$-band photometry to define flaring epochs and long-term activity states.

analysis.reason: The paper provides the first joint measurement of the cosmic matter density $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and dark energy equation of state $w$ using exclusively localized FRB dispersion measures, directly advancing FRB dispersion modeling and cosmological applications.
analysis.result: Using 125 localized FRBs at $0.105 \le z \le 2.148$, the authors obtain $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ in the flat $w$CDM model with BBN priors. In flat $\Lambda$CDM, $H_0 = 66.49^{+6.99}_{-6.43}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.27^{+0.09}_{-0.07}$. In flat $w_0 w_a$CDM, $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.33 \pm 0.10$, $w_0 = -0.65^{+0.43}_{-0.57}$, and $w_a = -0.78^{+1.26}$. The $\Omega_{\rm m}-w$ parameter degeneracy shows a positive correlation coefficient of $+0.54$, orthogonal to SNe Ia ($-0.94$), because increasing $\Omega_{\rm m}$ reduces $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}\rangle$ while enhancing $\sigma_{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}}$, whereas increasing $w$ reduces both.
analysis.problem: Deriving robust, standalone cosmological parameter constraints on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and $w$ using only localized FRBs without relying on external SNe Ia, BAO, or CMB measurements, while accounting for cosmic variance and host galaxy dispersion measure contributions.
analysis.method: Bayesian inference with PyMultiNest on 125 localized FRBs ($0.105 \le z \le 2.148$) with selection cuts $z > 0.1$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm exgal} > 5\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$. Total DM is decomposed as $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm obs}(z) = \mathrm{DM}_{\rm MW,ISM} + \mathrm{DM}_{\rm MW,halo} + \mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}(z) + \frac{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}}{1+z}$, where $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}(z_s)\rangle = \int_0^{z_s} \frac{c W(z)\,\mathrm{d}z}{H(z)}$ with weight function $W(z) = \frac{3\Omega_b H_0^2 \chi_e f_{\rm d}(z)(1+z)}{8\pi G m_p}$ (calibrated via TNG300) and variance $\sigma_{\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cos}}^2(z_s) \simeq \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{z_s} \frac{c\,\mathrm{d}z}{H(z)} W^2(z) \int_0^\infty \mathrm{d}k\,k\,P_{ee}(k,z)$ under the Limber and flat-sky approximations.
assumptions: Baseline Galactic halo dispersion measure contribution is assumed to be $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm MW,halo} = 50\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, with stability verified against directional models (YT20, L26, Y25).
limits: Restricted to localized FRBs with $z > 0.1$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm exgal} > 5\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ to mitigate non-Gaussian tail effects, peculiar velocities, and Galactic foreground uncertainties.

analysis.reason: This paper establishes the largest FAST burst-cluster catalog for the active repeating FRB 20240114A, providing vital empirical constraints on local magneto-ionic environment evolution (secular $\dot{\mathrm{DM}}$) and multi-timescale burst clustering directly relevant to repeating FRB central engines and PRS interactions.
analysis.result: The catalog comprises $13261$ burst clusters, $19037$ bursts, and $29026$ sub-bursts over $495$ days ($58.83$ hr exposure in 99 sessions). A weighted linear fit yields a secular DM increase rate of $\dot{\mathrm{DM}} = 1.29 \pm 0.11~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, while single-day DM shows an intra-day median of $528.4~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ (IQR $528.1$--$528.8~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$), confirming that broad single-day DM spreads in literature are morphology-induced pseudo-DM. Downward-to-upward drifting cluster ratio is $\approx 9.4:1$ with median drifting rates $R_{\rm d} = -27.7~\mathrm{MHz\,ms^{-1}}$ (D2-M) and $7.0~\mathrm{MHz\,ms^{-1}}$ (U2-M). Waiting times follow a three-component log-normal distribution with characteristic timescales $e^\mu \approx 2.34~\mathrm{ms}$, $24.83~\mathrm{ms}$, and $7.57~\mathrm{s}$ (inter-cluster, $\delta > 0.4~\mathrm{s}$), where cluster arrivals align with a variable-rate Poisson process. Characteristic emission frequencies correlate between FAST and Parkes ($r = 0.56, p = 5.3 \times 10^{-5}$) across a $112.91$-day modulation. Normalized burst cluster energy scales monotonically with multiplicity $N_{\rm sub}$ (Spearman $\rho = 0.895$--$1.000$), with higher energies observed during active phases and in complex/downward-drifting morphologies.

analysis.problem: Investigating the hierarchical multi-timescale emission morphology, spectral-temporal drifting physics, burst energetics, and distinguishing true secular circum-burst DM evolution from morphology-induced pseudo-DM in the active repeating source FRB 20240114A.
analysis.method: Analysis of 495-day monitoring using FAST L-band 19-beam receiver (center beam), utilizing TransientX and PSRCHIVE for pulse search and data reduction. Bursts within a $400~\mathrm{ms}$ window are grouped into burst clusters, followed by manual DM optimization in steps of $0.1~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ for $N_{\rm sub} \geq 2$ clusters, coupled with Weibull and log-normal waiting-time statistics.

Panel (a) shows the daily FAST sub-burst, burst, and burst-cluster rates and the cumulative FAST observing time. For reference, the Parkes/Murriyang burst rate derived from its full-band UWL data is also shown and is scaled by a factor of eight for display [ 50 ]. Panel (b) shows the morphology fractions in 10-day bins, with the corresponding time-integrated class counts on the right. Panels (c), (d), and (e) show the duration, Manual DM, and drifting rate, respectively, for burst clusters with $N_{\rm sub}\geq 2$, with panels (c) and (d) using the full sample and panel (e) only clusters exhibiting drifting behavior; the right-hand histograms show the corresponding distributions over the full observing span, with the median and 25th-75th percentile ranges indicated. Solid curves trace the daily statistics, grey dashed segments bridge missing-data gaps, and, in the relevant panels, purple and brown dash-dotted lines mark the linear- and log-space global means, respectively.

figures.physical_core: Tracks the 495-day long-term multi-parameter evolution of FRB 20240114A, including burst-cluster rates, morphology fractions, duration, drift rates, and a secular dispersion measure increase of $\mathrm{d(DM)/d}t = 1.29 \pm 0.11\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, providing critical observational constraints on circumburst medium evolution and emission geometry.

figures.caption: Figure 8: Energy dependence on burst-cluster multiplicity and activity state. Panels (a)–(c) show $E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N(\mathrm{BurstID})$, $E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N_{\mathrm{burst}}$, and $E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N_{\mathrm{sub}}$ as functions of counts. Grey points represent burst clusters, while open circles, open squares, and error bars denote the median, arithmetic mean, and 25th–75th percentile range, respectively. The median values are connected, and Spearman correlations are calculated from count-bin medians over $N(\mathrm{BurstID})\leq 6$, $N_{\mathrm{burst}}\leq 7$, and $N_{\mathrm{sub}}\leq 17$. Panels (d)–(f) compare energy-per-count measures among clusters with $N_{\mathrm{sub}}=1$, U2/m, ND2/m, D2/m, and C classifications. Blue and red points correspond to sessions with $R_{\mathrm{cluster}}<200~\mathrm{hr}^{-1}$ and $R_{\mathrm{cluster}}\geq 200~\mathrm{hr}^{-1}$, respectively.

figures.physical_core: Quantifies the dependence of cluster energy measures ($E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N(\mathrm{BurstID})$, $E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N_{\mathrm{burst}}$, and $E_{\mathrm{cluster}}/N_{\mathrm{sub}}$) on event counts, morphological classes, and activity rates ($R_{\mathrm{cluster}} < 200\,\mathrm{hr}^{-1}$ vs. $R_{\mathrm{cluster}} \geq 200\,\mathrm{hr}^{-1}$), revealing how burst energetics scale with cluster multiplicity.

analysis.reason: This study critically assesses candidate second-scale periodicities in repeating FRBs and demonstrates that non-Poissonian burst clustering and waiting-time statistics spuriously mimic coherent periodic signals.
analysis.result: Candidate short periods such as $P \sim 1.78\text{ s}$ with nominal Poisson significance of $3.62\sigma$ in FRB 20201124A (and conflicting peaks reaching up to $5.2\sigma$) clustering around $1\text{--}10\text{ s}$ across four active repeaters (FRB 20121102A, FRB 20201124A, FRB 20220912A, and FRB 20240114A) are reproduced by time-shuffled surrogate sequences preserving empirical waiting-time statistics. In ETAS simulations, varying the injected rotation period does not shift the recovered candidate recurrence distribution, showing that standard Poisson false-alarm calibration $p_{\rm FAP} = N_{\rm sim}(S_{\rm max} \geq S_{\rm obs}) / N_{\rm sim}$ severely overestimates detection significance.
analysis.problem: Whether reported second-scale candidate periodicities (e.g., $P \sim 1.78\text{ s}$) in repeating FRBs represent true magnetar spin modulation or spurious artifacts generated by burst clustering and non-Poisson waiting-time distributions under sliding-window searches.
analysis.method: Applied unbinned Rayleigh statistics $Z_{m}^{2}(P) = \frac{2}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{m}\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\cos k\phi_{i}\right)^{2} + \left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\sin k\phi_{i}\right)^{2}\right]$ with phase folding $\phi_{i} = \frac{(t_{i}-t_{0}) \bmod P}{P}$ and de Jager $H$-test $H(P) = \max_{1 \leq m \leq 5}[Z_{m}^{2}(P) - 4m + 4]$ across sliding windows of $N = 20\text{--}30$ bursts in the period range $0.01\text{ s} \leq P \leq 100\text{ s}$, combined with $10^{7}$ homogeneous Poisson Monte Carlo runs ($p_{\rm single} = \exp(-Z_{1}^{2}/2)$), model-independent waiting-time randomization, and Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) point-process simulations.
citation_leads: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering: “The randomized sequences reproduce the main candidate-period structures seen in the data”
IV.3 Waiting Time Randomization Test: “overall structure of the candidate-period distribution is closely coupled to the waiting-time statistics of the bursts”
IV.4 ETAS simulation: “the recurrence distribution of the recovered period candidates remains essentially unchanged”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes that burst clustering and non-Poisson waiting times naturally generate false periodicities in the $1\text{--}10\text{ s}$ range with apparent nominal significances exceeding $3\sigma$ (up to $5.2\sigma$), demonstrating that homogeneous Poisson null models are invalid for evaluating FRB periodicity and requiring future searches to calibrate significance against waiting-time-matched null models.

analysis.reason: This paper presents systematic searches for periodic activity in repeating FRBs using the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 and targeted observations of FRB 20240209A, uncovering four candidate activity periods that constrain repeating FRB progenitor models and emission geometry.
analysis.result: Identified a candidate activity period of $P = 170.4 \pm 4.7\ \mathrm{days}$ ($5.3\sigma$ post-trials) for FRB 20240209A with duty cycle $\delta = 0.89 \pm 0.02$ and active phase window $\phi = 0.34\text{--}0.76$ (enclosing $75\%$ of bursts within $42\%$ of the cycle), ruling out the previously reported $128.5\ \mathrm{day}$ period at $5.5\sigma$, while finding its period derivative $\dot{P} = 0.20 \pm 0.04\ \mathrm{day\ day^{-1}}$ very tentative. Uncovered three additional candidate periods from CHIME/FRB Catalog 2: FRB 20190208A with $P = 28.46 \pm 0.08\ \mathrm{days}$ ($3.1\sigma$, $\delta = 0.646 \pm 0.002$), FRB 20200926A with $P = 86.7 \pm 0.5\ \mathrm{days}$ ($4.0\sigma$, $\delta = 0.162 \pm 0.001$), and FRB 20220529A with $P = 36.4 \pm 0.5\ \mathrm{days}$ ($3.5\sigma$), alongside confirming FRB 20180916B at $P = 16.335 \pm 0.008\ \mathrm{days}$ ($13.8\sigma$, $\dot{P} = -1.3^{+4.0}_{-4.0} \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{day\ day^{-1}}$).
analysis.problem: Investigating whether long-term periodic bursting activity is a generic property of repeating FRBs, testing physical mechanisms (neutron star precession, binary orbital modulation, or intrinsic magnetar active episodes), and resolving ambiguities caused by sparse arrival times and survey exposure window aliasing.
analysis.method: Implemented a periodicity search pipeline across trial frequency range $[f_{\mathrm{min}}, f_{\mathrm{max}}] = [3/T, 1/P_{\mathrm{min}}]$ ($P_{\mathrm{min}} = 10\ \mathrm{days}$, oversampling factor $O = 5$) using Lomb-Scargle, weighted Rayleigh ($Z_1^2$), and weighted $H$-test statistics; assessed significance via $N_{\mathrm{sim}} = 10^9$ Monte Carlo simulations under an exposure-modulated homogeneous Poisson null model, with aliasing evaluated via $f_{\mathrm{alias}} = |f \pm m f_{\mathrm{sid}}|$ and exposure window power at $f_{\mathrm{w}} = 1/(306.6\ \mathrm{days})$.
assumptions: Statistical significances and false-alarm probabilities assume a homogeneous (constant-rate) Poisson null hypothesis modulated by the CHIME daily exposure function.
limits: Significances may decrease under burst clustering null models, apparent period derivatives remain tentative without confirmed physical precedent, and daily meridian transit sampling induces sidereal aliasing that requires off-transit pointed verification.

analysis.reason: Directly investigates supernova shock breakout and cooling emission in dense circumstellar material shells to model extragalactic fast X-ray transients such as EP260321a, aligning directly with the group's core focus on shock breakout and CSM interaction.
analysis.result: For typical parameters ($v_{\mathrm{sh}} \sim 0.1\,c$, $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} = 10^{-4}\,M_\odot$, $r_{\mathrm{out}} = 10^{13}\,\mathrm{cm}$), thermal coupling yields $\eta \approx 4$ and a Comptonized color temperature $T_{\mathrm{col,SBO}} \approx 0.127\,\mathrm{keV}$, naturally generating soft X-ray transients with peak luminosities $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{45}-10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. MCMC modeling of EP260321a ($z=0.0344$) reproduces its observed peak luminosity of $(1.0\pm 0.3)\times 10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $(690\pm 60)\,\mathrm{s}$ with blackbody temperature $\sim 0.1-0.13\,\mathrm{keV}$, establishing it as the first confirmed non-relativistic shock breakout EFXT.
analysis.reading_entry: III Shock Breakout and Cooling Lightcurve
analysis.problem: Investigates whether shock breakout and post-breakout cooling emission in a pre-explosion dense circumstellar material shell can comprehensively explain extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) like EP260321a, XRF 060218, and XRO 080109 without invoking relativistic jets.
analysis.method: Constructs a semi-analytical radiation-mediated shock model in a spherical thin CSM shell ($M_{\mathrm{CSM}}$, $r_{\mathrm{out}}$, $\chi \equiv (r_{\mathrm{out}}-r_{\mathrm{in}})/r_{\mathrm{out}} \ll 1$, $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim M_{\mathrm{CSM}}/(4\pi r_{\mathrm{out}}^3 \chi)$) driven by SN ejecta with shock velocity $v_{\mathrm{sh}} \approx 0.1\,E_{\mathrm{kin},51}^{1/2}(M_{\mathrm{ej}}/2\,M_\odot)^{-5/14}(M_{\mathrm{CSM}}/10^{-4}\,M_\odot)^{-1/7}c$. Incorporates non-LTE Comptonization color-temperature correction ($T_{\mathrm{col}} = T_{\mathrm{BB}}\eta^2/\xi^2$ when coupling parameter $\eta \approx n_{\mathrm{BB}}/[t_{\mathrm{diff}}\dot{n}_{\mathrm{ph,ff}}(T_{\mathrm{BB}})] > 1$) and integrates over equal-arrival-time surfaces $t = t_{\mathrm{obs}} - [\max(r_{\mathrm{out}}, r_{\mathrm{sh}})/c](1-\cos\theta)$ to account for light-travel time effects.
assumptions: Shock heating and cooling emission uniformly heat all material exterior to the diffusion front.

analysis.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch optical spectroscopic monitoring of the microquasar SS433 to constrain small periodic velocity and directional deviations in its relativistic jets. It establishes a perturbation expansion framework explaining these periodicities via tidal perturbations and dynamical gas stream interactions with the precessing disk.
analysis.result: The mean relativistic jet speed is $\bar{\beta} = 0.2562 \pm 0.0004$, exhibiting orbital modulation at $P = 13.083\,\mathrm{d}$ with velocity amplitude $\Delta\beta = (6.0 \pm 0.6) \times 10^{-3}$ (peaking at orbital phase $\varphi = 0.334 \pm 0.015$) and a combination frequency $(\omega+2\Omega)$ modulation at $P = 11.267\,\mathrm{d}$ with $\Delta\beta = (4.5 \pm 0.5) \times 10^{-3}$. Directional deviations exhibit periodicities in redshift at $P = 6.2870\,\mathrm{d}$ (nutation, $\Delta z = (9.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$), $P = 5.8342\,\mathrm{d}$ ($(2\omega+3\Omega)$, $\Delta z = (3.2 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$), and a newly detected period at $P = 3.0830\,\mathrm{d}$ ($(4\omega+3\Omega)$, $\Delta z = (2.0 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-3}$). The line-of-sight velocity perturbation scales as $\Delta z \approx \gamma\beta a(\mu) \mathbf{d}\cdot\mathbf{I} = \gamma\beta \sum_{k} a_k \mu^k \cos(\varphi - \varphi_k) \sin i$.
analysis.problem: Relativistic jets in SS433 systematically deviate from standard kinematic precession and nutation models, exhibiting both independent random angular jitter ($\sigma \lesssim 1.5^{\circ}$) breaking strict antiparallelism and harmonic velocity/directional periodicities whose dynamical origins require quantitative explanation.
analysis.method: Analysis of 461 optical spectra ($3550\text{--}7450\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) obtained with the Caucasus Mountain Observatory 2.5-m telescope (2020–2026) across Balmer and He I lines ($5876, 6678, 7065\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$) to measure $z^{\pm}$. Jet speed is determined via transverse Doppler effect $\beta = \sqrt{1 - [1 + (z_- + z_+)/2]^{-2}}$, and trajectory perturbations are modeled via power-series expansion $a(\mu) = \sum_k a_k \mu^k$ where $\mu_\pm = \mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{j}^\pm = \pm \sin\theta \cos(\varphi + \psi)$.
assumptions: Assuming that the velocities in both jets are equal in magnitude and strictly opposite in direction when computing individual values of $\beta$ from the transverse Doppler effect.
limits: The predicted $(3\omega+2\Omega)$ periodicity at $4.14\,\mathrm{d}$ remained undetectable due to small predicted amplitude ($\approx 1.3 \times 10^{-3}$), emission-line decay damping (timescale $\sim 1\,\mathrm{d}$), and random phase noise.

analysis.reason: SN 2017gkk is a fast-evolving, moderately luminous Type IIb stripped-envelope supernova that provides quantitative observational constraints on core-collapse explosion parameters, 56Ni production, and progenitor envelope stripping mechanisms.
analysis.result: The event reached a peak absolute magnitude $M_V = -17.01 \pm 0.07\,\mathrm{mag}$ with rise time $t_{\rm rise}(V) = 13.09_{-0.74}^{+0.71}\,\mathrm{days}$ at $D_{\mathrm{L}} = 19.05 \pm 0.59\,\mathrm{Mpc}$. Peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity is $L_{\rm bol} = (8.37 \pm 0.19) \times 10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and black-body bolometric peak is $L_{\rm bol, BB} = (2.15 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ via $L_{\mathrm{Bol,BB}} = 4\pi R_{\mathrm{BB}}^2 \sigma T_{\mathrm{BB}}^4$. Post-peak decline is rapid with $\gamma_{25<t<80}(V) = 2.35 \pm 0.06\,\mathrm{mag\times(100\,days)^{-1}}$. Analytical modeling yields ejecta mass $M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 1.38_{-0.31}^{+0.48}\,M_\odot$, nickel mass fraction $f_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.055_{-0.012}^{+0.013}$, ejecta velocity $v_{\mathrm{ej}} = 9120_{-410}^{+430}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, and $\gamma$-ray leakage timescale $t_{\rm leak} = 59.57_{-2.02}^{+2.10}\,\mathrm{days}$ (opacity $\kappa_\gamma = 0.033_{-0.010}^{+0.011}\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}$). Late-time line flux ratio $[\mathrm{Ca\ II}]/[\mathrm{O\ I}] = 1.686_{-0.130}^{+0.145}$ and oxygen mass $M_{\mathrm{O}} \approx 0.023\,M_\odot$ from $M_{\mathrm{O}} = 10^8 d_{\mathrm{L}}^2 f([\mathrm{O\,I}]) \times \exp(2.28/T_4)\,M_\odot$ constrain the progenitor zero-age main-sequence mass to $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}} \approx 12\,M_\odot$.
analysis.problem: Investigating the progenitor physical nature, envelope stripping channel (single-star stellar wind vs. binary interaction), explosion energetics, and 56Ni mixing in the fast-evolving Type IIb stripped-envelope core-collapse supernova SN 2017gkk.
analysis.method: Optical BVRI photometry and low-resolution spectroscopy reduction with template image subtraction; bolometric light curve synthesis via black-body SED fitting governed by $L_{\mathrm{Bol,BB}} = 4\pi R_{\mathrm{BB}}^2 \sigma T_{\mathrm{BB}}^4$; semi-analytical radioactive decay diffusion modeling of $^{56}\mathrm{Ni} \rightarrow {}^{56}\mathrm{Co}$; and nebular forbidden-line diagnostic modeling calibrated by NLTE radiative transfer models and oxygen mass scaling $M_{\mathrm{O}} = 10^8 d_{\mathrm{L}}^2 f([\mathrm{O\,I}]) \times \exp(2.28/T_4)\,M_\odot$.
limits: Early photometric data coverage is sparse, rendering the extrapolated explosion epoch and rising time uncertain.

analysis.reason: This paper introduces a high-dimensional lattice shortest vector problem (SVP) algorithm for blind gamma-ray pulsar searches, overcoming severe computational bottlenecks and discovering the isolated millisecond pulsar PSR J1622−7204 from Fermi-LAT observations.
analysis.result: The lattice-based search identified PSR J1622−7204 with false-alarm probability $p \approx \exp(-0.4 H) \approx 10^{-40}$ and test statistic $H \sim 345$, using $N_{\gamma} = 15,905$ photon events ($w_i > 0.01$) yielding an effective photon weight $\sum_i w_i \approx 828$ and pulsation significance metric $\sum_i w_i^2 \approx 193$.
analysis.problem: Blind coherent searches for faint gamma-ray pulsars in sparse-photon regimes ($\,\lesssim 10^3$ photons over $10^9\text{--}10^{11}$ rotations) require $\sim 10^{22}$ trial points due to timing modulations from spin-down and detector motion, rendering brute-force approaches computationally intractable.
analysis.method: The search maps linearized photon arrival times under the quadratic spin-down model $\Phi(\tau) = \phi_0 + f\tau + \frac{1}{2}\dot{f}\tau^2$ and parameters $\mathbf{p} = [\phi_0, f, \dot{f}, f\Delta\alpha, f\Delta\delta]$ with integer rotations $\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ into an $n$-dimensional lattice shortest nonzero vector problem, solved via block Korkine-Zolotarev reduction.

analysis.reason: This work directly investigates the central engine nature of long GRBs with X-ray plateaus by distinguishing collapsar black holes from magnetars using multimessenger gravitational wave signatures and accretion evolution.
analysis.result: MCMC fitting of X-ray plateaus under the collapsar black hole spin-down model yields initial black hole masses $M_{\rm BH} \sim 24\text{--}124\,M_{\odot}$ and accretion disc masses $M_{\rm disc} \sim 0.1\,M_{\rm BH}$ (e.g., GRB 080319C has $M_0 = 123.5 \pm 3.7\,M_{\odot}$, $\log_{10}(\dot{M}/[M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}]) = -1.83 \pm 0.03$, $M_{\mathrm{disc}} = 12.0 \pm 0.8\,M_{\odot}$). In a pessimistic scenario (efficiency $\epsilon = 0.1$), the characteristic gravitational wave strains at $\sim 200\,\mathrm{Hz}$ are $h_c \sim (1.5\text{--}1.84) \times 10^{-24}$, placing them on the detection threshold of Cosmic Explorer with an expected detection rate of $0.5\text{--}1.5\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. In contrast, a white dwarf tidal disruption event (WD-TDE) around an intermediate-mass black hole ($M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^5\,M_{\odot}$) emits at $f_{\rm peak} \simeq 1.6 f_c = \frac{1.6}{2\pi}\sqrt{G M_{\rm BH}/r_t^3} < 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, falling in the decihertz band detectable by DECIGO/BBO.
analysis.reading_entry: IV Detectability of GWs from collapsar-origin BHs
analysis.problem: The identity and energy-injection mechanism of the central engines powering long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with X-ray plateaus—specifically whether they are driven by accreting/non-accreting magnetars or Kerr black holes via accretion and Blandford-Znajek spin-down—remain degenerate from electromagnetic observations alone.
analysis.method: The authors model collapsar black hole evolution governed by coupled accretion and Blandford-Znajek torque equations, $\frac{dM_{\rm BH}}{dt} = e_{\rm in}\dot{M} - \frac{L_{\rm BZ}}{c^2}$ and $\frac{da}{dt} = \frac{c}{G M_{\rm BH}^2}(l_{\rm in}\dot{M} - T_{\rm BZ})$, distinguishing turbulent disc broadband emission (Model A) from descending chirps (Model B) and magnetar spin-down (Model C). Black hole parameters are derived via MCMC fitting of Swift/XRT afterglow light curves and mapped to GW strain spectra $h_c(f)$ for 3G ground-based and space-borne detectors.
limits: Gravitational waves from collapsar discs in pessimistic efficiency regimes ($\epsilon \sim 0.1$) fall near the sensitivity limits of Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope, requiring 3G detectors for firm detection.

analysis.reason: Provides the largest systematic 3D GR$\nu$RMHD simulation suite of stellar-mass black hole accretion disks to date, establishing key scaling laws for Blandford-Znajek jet power, ejecta properties, and nucleosynthesis relevant to central engines and kilonovae.
analysis.result: Blandford-Znajek peak jet power scales with disk mass as $P_{\rm jet,max} = 10^{52} \left(M_{\rm disk}/M_\odot\right)^{0.82}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ (steepening to index $1.61$ above $\log(M_{\rm disk}/M_\odot) > -1.5$), while $\dot{M}_{\rm peak}$ does not strictly scale one-to-one with $M_{\rm disk}$. Ejecta mass reaches an extrapolated fraction of $\sim 50\%$, with average radial velocity $\langle v_r/c \rangle \sim 0.07$ and final electron fraction $0.16 \le \langle Y_{\rm e} \rangle \le 0.50$.
analysis.problem: Determining how central engine outflows, jet launching efficiency, and heavy-element nucleosynthesis quantitatively scale across a wide parameter space of black hole accretion disks, and providing physically calibrated spatial $Y_{\rm e}$ distributions for downstream kilonova modeling.
analysis.method: Carries out 25 three-dimensional GR$\nu$RMHD simulations using $\nu$bhlight, solving general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics with Monte Carlo neutrino transport in stationary Kerr spacetimes, combined with Gaussian Process active parameter space exploration and PRISM nuclear reaction network calculations.

limits: Only Disks 1, 4, and 6 produce meaningful amounts of actinides ($X_{\rm Ac} > 10^{-4}$).

analysis.reason: This paper establishes the first nonlinearly causal and strongly hyperbolic formulation of general-relativistic two-fluid superfluid hydrodynamics incorporating vortex line tension and constrained transport, providing a rigorous mathematical and numerical foundation for modeling neutron star interior vortex dynamics, glitches, and potential triggers for magnetar giant flares and fast radio bursts.
analysis.result:
The framework successfully reproduces the long-wavelength Kelvin wave dispersion $|\omega| \simeq  rac{\mathcal{T}k^2}{\kappa_v 
u}$ (where $
u = 
u_n + \mathcal{Z}n_p$) along a vortex column within $1.3\%$ error of analytic predictions (yielding dispersion ratio $\omega(0.4)/\omega(0.2) = 4.24$ vs. theoretical $4.264$). In nonrotating relativistic neutron star oscillation benchmarks ($M = 1.47137\,M_\odot, R_s = 11.0866\,\mathrm{km}$), it accurately resolves two-fluid fundamental modes $\omega_{n,F}t_u = 0.74439$ ($3.552\,\mathrm{kHz}$ for $t_u \approx 33.36\,\mu\mathrm{s}$) and $\omega_{p,F}t_u = 1.13242$. In global $500\,\mathrm{Hz}$ rotating neutron star simulations, spin-down drives poloidal circulation transport beyond the unpinning threshold $\Lambda = \ell_{m num}/ ar{f}_c > 1$ with critical rotation lag $\Delta\Omega_{m crit} \simeq  rac{\alpha f_c}{ho_{n,m rest}\kappa_{m vel}\varpi}$, creating an angular momentum deficit $ rac{\mathrm{d}\Delta J_n}{\mathrm{d}R} = -\partial_R \int_0^t \mathcal{F}_n\,\mathrm{d}t' + \int_0^t \mathcal{T}_n\,\mathrm{d}t'$ peaking at $R \simeq 0.47 L_0$ and leaving a persistent differentially rotating superfluid state.
analysis.problem: Traditional force-equilibrium models for superfluid vortex dynamics in neutron star interiors suffer from a fatal loss of strong hyperbolicity and non-causal ill-posedness driven by the short-wavelength limit of the Donnelly–Glaberson instability in three-dimensional dissipative counterflow, preventing stable, physically consistent multidimensional general-relativistic simulations of vortex unpinning and angular momentum transfer.
analysis.method: The authors formulate a 14-moment Carter multifluid framework in $3+1$ general relativity with metric $\mathrm{d}s^2 = -\alpha^2 \mathrm{d}t^2 + \gamma_{ij}(\mathrm{d}x^i + \beta^i \mathrm{d}t)(\mathrm{d}x^j + \beta^j \mathrm{d}t)$, regularized by vortex line tension $\mathcal{T} = F_{\mathcal{N}}$ derived from an energy density $F(\nu_n, n_p, \mathcal{N}) = A_\Omega \mathcal{N}[L_\Omega + \alpha_{\rm v}\mathcal{N}/(2\mathcal{N}_0)]$. They exploit a mathematical analogy with force-free electrodynamics (FFE) to define effective fields $E_\mu, B^\mu$ and drift velocity $\bm{v}_{L\perp} = (\bm{E} \times \bm{B})/B^2$, implementing a flux-conservative scheme with constrained transport for $\nabla_i B^i = 0$, IMEX Runge–Kutta time integration with local backward-Euler solves for stiff dissipation, WENO-Z spatial reconstruction with HLL fluxes, and a 5-variable damped quasi-Newton primitive recovery algorithm enforcing strict causal bounds ($S > 0, U \succeq 0$).
assumptions: Local charge neutrality where electrons comove with charged proton carriers, suppressing explicit electromagnetic plasma degrees of freedom.
limits: Evolution remains valid only within the domain of strong hyperbolicity and nonlinear causality ($S > 0, U \succeq 0$), which sets strict algebraic bounds on relative counterflow Lorentz factor $g < G$ and vortex slip velocity.

analysis.reason: This study models the Galactic population of dormant neutron star binaries and forecasts Gaia DR4/DR5 astrometric yields, providing quantitative constraints on core-collapse supernova engines, natal kicks, and dense matter equations of state.
analysis.result: Under the realistic selection function gaiamock, Gaia is predicted to detect $\sim 100\text{--}110$ and $\sim 300\text{--}380$ dormant neutron star--luminous companion (NS--LC) binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively. In the intrinsic population, $\sim 94\%$ of surviving detached systems survive through common envelope (CE) evolution ($P_{\rm orb} \le 10\,\mathrm{yr}$). The observed NS mass distribution peaks sharply at $1.2\text{--}1.3\,M_\odot$ driven by low-kick ($\sigma = 20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) electron-capture supernovae (ECSN), while delayed core-collapse supernova (CCSN) fallback produces massive NSs exceeding $M_{\rm NS} > 2.5\,M_\odot$ in $\sim 1\%$ of systems. Pulsar spin-down and magnetic field decay follow $\dot{P}_{\rm spin} = K \frac{B^2}{P_{\rm spin}}$ ($K = 9.87 \times 10^{-48}\,\mathrm{yr\,G^{-2}}$), death line $B/P_{\rm spin}^2 = 0.17 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{G\,s^{-2}}$, and accretion-induced burial $B = \frac{B_0}{1 + \Delta M / (10^{-6}\,M_\odot)} \exp\left(-\frac{T - t_{\rm acc}}{\tau}\right)$ with $\tau = 3\,\mathrm{Gyr}$.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the Galactic population of dormant neutron stars in detached binaries with luminous companions (NS--LC) detectable via astrometric orbital wobbles in Gaia DR4 and DR5, and testing whether their yields and orbital parameters can break degeneracies between core-collapse supernova explosion models (rapid vs. delayed), natal kicks ($\sigma = 265\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs. $20\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), and common envelope evolution.
analysis.method: Binary population synthesis using COSMIC initialized with a Kroupa IMF ($3 < m_{\rm pri}/M_\odot < 60$), flat mass ratios ($q = m_{\rm sec}/m_{\rm pri}$), thermal eccentricities, and log-flat semi-major axes up to $10^5\,R_\odot$. Spatial distribution and star formation histories are drawn from the FIRE-2 m12i Milky Way simulation ($10^{-4} \le Z \le 0.03$). Supernova prescriptions incorporate rapid and delayed core-collapse models (maximum $M_{\rm NS} = 3\,M_\odot$), ECSN ($M_{\rm ZAMS} \sim 8\text{--}10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ch} \approx 1.38\,M_\odot$), and accretion-induced collapse (AIC), followed by synthetic observation through CCB22 and gaiamock astrometric selection functions.
assumptions: The Milky Way binary population follows star formation and metallicity distributions from the FIRE-2 m12i simulation evaluated across 100 Galactic realizations.
limits: The isolated binary evolution models produce no detached millisecond pulsars (MSPs) with main-sequence companions, in contrast to 29 known field radio MSPs in tight orbits from the ATNF pulsar catalog.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a unified Poynting-flux-dominated jet model connecting fast X-ray transients (FXTs) to gamma-ray bursts via premature magnetic dissipation when the jet satisfies the causal condition $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$.
analysis.result: Premature kink instability dissipates Poynting flux at stellar breakout radius $R_* \sim 10^{11}\,\mathrm{cm}$ with Lorentz factor $\Gamma \sim 20$, yielding rapid thermalization where mean comoving photon energy $\langle E' \rangle \sim 2.7 k_{\rm B} [L_{\rm iso}/(4\pi R_*^2 \Gamma^2 a c)]^{1/4} \sim 0.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ escapes as soft X-rays with thermalization timescale $\tau_{\rm th} \sim N_{\rm th} R_* / (\ell' c)$, minimum variability timescale $\Delta t_{\rm var} \simeq (1+z) R_{\rm ph} \theta_{\rm J}^2 / (2c) \sim 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}$, and no jet breaks because $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma < 1$ holds throughout.
analysis.problem: Explaining the physical nature of fast X-ray transients (FXTs) associated with type Ic-BL supernovae that exhibit soft thermal X-ray spectra, low peak energies, long deceleration times, and an absence of geometric jet breaks.
analysis.method: Modeling Blandford–Znajek driven Poynting-flux-dominated jets with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \gg 1$ accelerating via ideal MHD magnetic pressure gradient as $\Gamma(R) = \sigma_0^{3/2}(R/R_{\rm sat})^{1/3}$, where global kink instability triggers premature dissipation at $R_*$ if $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R_*) < 1$.
assumptions: The relativistic jet is Poynting-flux dominated with initial magnetization $\sigma_0 \equiv \dot{E}_{\rm Poynting}/\dot{E}_{\rm kinetic} \gg 1$ accelerating as $\Gamma(R) \propto R^{1/3}$ before saturation.
limits: Global kink instability requires the entire jet cross-section to remain causally connected under $\theta_{\rm J}\Gamma(R) < 1$.

In the sketch, we also plot the case when the premature dissipation is absence, the jet continues accelerating to ultra-relativistic Lorentz factor and produces a classical gamma-ray burst (GRB) via dissipation at larger radii.

analysis.reason: This paper presents an unprecedented, continuously monitored common envelope evolution event and stellar merger in M31 (AT 2025abao), directly probing circumstellar material (CSM) interaction and plateau emission mechanisms relevant to shock interaction and plateau studies in transients.
analysis.result: The progenitor is identified as an early AGB star ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $R_{\rm eff} \approx 350\,R_\odot$, $L \approx 1.8 \times 10^4\,L_\odot$, $\dot{M} \approx 10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$) with a low-mass companion ($M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, mass ratio $q=0.10_{-0.08}^{+0.10}$). The 7-year precursor brightening ($L_{\rm drag} \approx 3 \times 10^{38}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$) was driven by frictional drag in the primary's convective envelope, transitioning to a dynamic plunge and luminous red nova eruption with ejecta kinetic energy $KE_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{48}\,{\rm erg}$ and unbound mass $\sim 0.2\text{--}0.4\,M_\odot$, whose optical plateau is powered by momentum-conserving shock interaction with equatorial CSM having $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$.
analysis.problem: How orbital energy is partitioned and dissipated during common envelope evolution (CEE), and whether standard $\alpha$-formalisms adequately describe envelope unbinding versus ejecta kinetic acceleration and shock interactions with pre-existing CSM.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch photometric monitoring (ZTF, WINTER, SPHEREx, Cerberus 1-second cadence) and spectroscopic follow-up (Gemini/GMOS, FIES, NIRES, JWST/MIRI MRS), combined with PHOENIX stellar atmosphere and DUSTY radiative transfer SED fitting via emcee MCMC, alongside momentum-conserving shock deceleration modeling of the ejecta-CSM interaction.

figures.caption: Figure 10: A graphical representation of the different phases of AT 2025abao. a) The quiescent binary system comprising a $\approx 7$ M ⊙ AGB and a $\approx 0.7$ M ⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b) The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for $\approx 7$ years. The mass outflow rate during this phase is $\sim 10^{-2}$ M ⊙ yr -1, producing $\sim 0.1$ M ⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown), c) The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of $\approx 0.1-0.2$ M ⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d) The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. The surviving pre-existing dust is traced by our JWST observations. The black arrows between the panels indicate the progression of time.
figures.label: Fig. 10
figures.physical_core: A four-stage schematic illustrating the full physical lifecycle of Common Envelope Evolution (CEE) in AT 2025abao: (a) the quiescent binary ($\approx 7\,M_\odot$ AGB primary and $\approx 0.7\,M_\odot$ companion) with pre-existing dust from Roche Lobe overflow; (b) a $\approx 7$-year precursor brightening powered by frictional drag dissipation during companion inspiral through the convective envelope ($\\dot{M} \sim 10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$); (c) ballistic envelope ejection ($\\approx 0.1\text{--}0.2\,M_\odot$) triggered by the core merger; and (d) subsequent shock interaction between merger ejecta and equatorial circumstellar matter.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Understanding CEE. Top Left: Peak precursor luminosity versus primary escape speed for AT 2025abao, V1309Sco [ 17 ], and M31-LRN-2015 [ 22 ], colored by precursor duration in orbital periods at the primary’s surface. Lines show the kinetic luminosity of outflows at various mass-loss rates (dashed gray, Equation 5 ) and drag luminosity from an inspiraling companion (red, Equation 7 ) for the mass ratios in the legend. Top right: Theoretical estimates of dust mass around the quiescent progenitor (black line: analytical, squares: MESA simulations) versus that ejected during the precursor (Section 1.4.3 ), colored by binary mass ratio. The shaded region spans the progenitor dust range by varying the analytical-model parameters (Section 1.4.2 ). The red star shows measured values with 1 $\sigma$ uncertainties. Bottom left: Envelope binding energy versus radius (black) from the MESA model of the 7 M ⊙, 340 R ⊙ AGB primary star, inferred orbital energy dissipated by the companion (red), observed ejecta kinetic energy (blue), and observed radiated energy during the precursor (green). Solid lines are median values, shaded regions mark 1 $\sigma$ uncertainties. Bottom Right: CE efficiency $\alpha$ versus binary mass ratio. The inferred mass ratio and its 1 $\sigma$ uncertainty is marked with the purple solid line and shaded region. Black shaded regions are ruled out by a core-merger in this system and its observed ejected mass. Black points show $\alpha$ measurements from post-CE binary systems [ 50 ] (Section 1.4.6 ).
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: Comprehensive theoretical and empirical diagnostic of CEE energetics and parameters: compares inspiral drag luminosity and outflow kinetic luminosity against precursor properties; contrasts the MESA primary envelope binding energy $E_{\mathrm{bind}}(r)$ with dissipated orbital energy $\Delta E_{\mathrm{orb}}$, ejecta kinetic energy $E_{\mathrm{kin}}$, and radiated energy $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$; and establishes empirical constraints on the common envelope efficiency parameter $0.01 \lesssim \alpha \lesssim 0.4$ as a function of binary mass ratio $q$.

analysis.reason: The paper develops a parameter-free, high-order smoothness indicator for AMR in Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations, demonstrating robust tracking of relativistic blast waves and black hole accretion flows with significant speedups.
analysis.result: The indicator accurately captures discontinuities and shear layers across tests: in Kelvin–Helmholtz instability tests with $\Gamma=5/3$ and effective resolution $2048^{2}$, it speeds up computation by $1.45\times$; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, it achieves a $3.4\times$ reduction in MeshBlock-cycles and $2.8\times$ wall-clock speedup; in GRMHD MAD simulations around Kerr black holes ($a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9, \phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH}/\sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$), it successfully resolves jet launching, though computational savings diminish when the region $r \le 100r_g$ becomes fully turbulent.
analysis.problem: High computational cost and lack of problem-independent, robust error indicators for adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) in multi-dimensional Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations.
analysis.method: Adapted from spectral modal falloff indicators, the scheme calculates the 4th-order undivided finite difference $\Delta^{(4)}u = u_{i+2}-4u_{i+1}+6u_{i}-4u_{i-1}+u_{i-2}$ over a symmetric 5-point stencil to obtain the oscillation measure $e_i = |\Delta^{(4)}u/u_i|$, applying fixed thresholds $4^{-2}=0.0625$ for refinement and $4^{-3}=0.015625$ for coarsening across conserved variables $(D, M^j, E, B^j)$ in AthenaK.
assumptions: Monitored physical fields are sufficiently smooth away from true discontinuities such that high-order polynomial modal coefficients decay rapidly.
limits: AMR computational savings diminish once turbulence fills the entire domain of interest (such as fully developed post-eruption MAD states at $r \le 100r_g$), and initial discontinuities require pre-refinement to prevent staircasing artifacts.

analysis.reason: This work discovers a GeV gamma-ray source spatially offset from SNR G21.8-3.0 and interacting with cavity molecular gas, constraining cosmic-ray acceleration and early suppressed transport in supernova circumstellar wind-blown bubbles.
analysis.result: Discovered an offset GeV gamma-ray source SrcT with LogParabola spectrum (photon index $\alpha = 0.59 \pm 0.18$, curvature $\beta = 0.28 \pm 0.06$, $\mathrm{TS_{curve}} = 46.7$) and flux $(1.35 \pm 0.27) \times 10^{-9}\ \mathrm{photon\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$, spatially matching a molecular cloud of mass $M \sim 101\,d_{0.8}^{2}\ M_{\odot}$ and density $n \sim 253\,d_{0.8}^{-1}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ outside a wind-blown cavity ($n_{\rm cavity} \sim 8\,d_{0.8}^{-1}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$); cosmic-ray diffusion within the cavity is suppressed by a factor of $\sim 30$ relative to standard Galactic diffusion.
analysis.reading_entry: III.2 Escaped Cosmic Rays and the Origin of the $gamma$-ray Excess
analysis.problem: SNR G21.8-3.0 shows non-thermal radio emission but lacks high-energy gamma-ray emission from the remnant shell itself, raising the question of where accelerated cosmic rays escape and how progenitor wind-blown cavity environments regulate their early diffusion.
analysis.method: Analyzed 16-yr Fermi-LAT 0.1–1000 GeV data testing spatial extension ($\mathrm{TS_{ext}} \sim 2\text{--}3$) and variability ($\mathrm{TS_{var}} = 7.9$), combined with MWISP $^{12}\mathrm{CO}\ (J=1-0)$ molecular line mapping at $v_{\rm LSR} \sim +9\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ and Weaver self-similar wind-driven bubble dynamics $t_{\rm c} = \frac{3}{5}\frac{R_{\rm c}}{v_{\rm c}} \simeq 9\times 10^5\left(\frac{R_{\rm c}}{7.0\,\mathrm{pc}}\right)\left(\frac{v_{\rm c}}{4.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}}\right)^{-1}\ \mathrm{yr}$ to model hadronic cosmic-ray illumination under suppressed Kraichnan or Bohm diffusion.
assumptions: A standard CO-to-$\mathrm{H_2}$ conversion factor $X_{\mathrm{CO}} = 2\times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}\ K^{-1}\ km^{-1}\ s}$ and distance $d = 0.8\ \mathrm{kpc}$ to infer molecular mass.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first binary population synthesis coupled with time-dependent synchrotron nebular models for hyper-Eddington mass-transfer systems, directly constraining persistent radio source (PRS) counterparts to repeating FRBs, relativistic jet inflation, and radio transient surveys.
analysis.result: The local volumetric birth rate of hyper-Eddington mass-transfer binaries is $\mathcal{R} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ spanning $\dot{m} \sim 10^{2\text{--}7}$ and accretion timescales $t_{\rm acc} \sim 10^{0\text{--}6}\,\mathrm{yr}$. The systems launch mildly relativistic jets ($v_{\rm j} \sim 0.1\text{--}0.3c$) and disk winds ($v_{\rm w} \sim 0.03c$) inflating long-lived synchrotron hypernebulae with peak radio luminosities $L_{\nu,\rm peak} \sim 10^{28}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\text{--}3\,\mathrm{GHz}$, overlapping with FRB-associated PRSs and yielding $\sim 10^{2\text{--}5}$ detectable steady sources in VLASS.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing unresolved synchrotron hypernebulae driven by rare, energetic hyper-Eddington binary mass transfer from other populations of unresolved synchrotron sources (such as AGNs, SNRs, and GRB afterglows) in modern wide-field radio surveys.
analysis.method: Coupled COMPAS binary population synthesis (v02.35.03) with a semi-analytic synchrotron hypernebula model. For stable RLOF, the mass-transfer rate is set by donor envelope thermal timescale $\dot{M} = \dot{M}_{\rm th} = M_{\rm d,env}/\tau_{\rm KH} = R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}/(G M_{\rm d})$ with duration $t_{\rm acc} = \tau_{\rm KH}$, whereas unstable common-envelope evolution incorporates pre-dynamical accretion $\dot{M} = f_{\rm acc}\Delta M_{\rm CE}/(100 P_{\rm orb})$. Jet kinetic luminosity scales as $L_{\rm j} = \eta L_{\rm w} \simeq \frac{1}{2}\eta \dot{M} v_{\rm w}^2$ with efficiency $\eta \sim 0.1$, injecting relativistic electrons at the termination shock.
assumptions: The donor star transfers its envelope onto a compact object (NS or BH) at hyper-Eddington rates $\dot{M} \gtrsim \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} \equiv L_{\rm Edd}/(0.1c^2)$.
limits: VLBI observations with milliarcsecond-scale resolution are insensitive to diffuse parsec-scale hypernebula structures.

analysis.reason: This paper provides valuable observational and theoretical constraints on neutron star crustal heating mechanisms by utilizing carbon burning instability to break the degeneracy between shallow and deep heating in KS 1731-260, offering key insights for compact object high-energy thermal evolution.
analysis.result: Enforcing the local carbon ignition instability criterion $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ breaks the degeneracy of quiescent cooling fits and strongly favors shallow heating overlapping the carbon fuel layer at column depth $y_* = 0.630\times 10^{12}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$. Deeper heating ($\log_{10}P = 27\text{--}28\text{ dyn cm}^{-2}$) requires nearly twice the heating strength ($q_a = 4.00\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ vs. $2.19\text{ MeV nucleon}^{-1}$ for shallow heating under CF88 rates), causing severe quiescent spectral residuals ($\Delta W \simeq 352$ vs. $\Delta W \simeq 39$) and overpredicting $2\text{--}3\text{ keV}$ counts by a factor of $\sim 5$. For the superburst decay at $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$, depth-dependent energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^{1/4}$ with $y_{\rm h} = 6.62\times 10^{11}\text{ g cm}^{-2}$ and total burst energy $\mathcal{E}_{\rm b} = 2.19\times 10^{42}\text{ erg}$ (residual sum 10.2) reproduces early cooling significantly better than uniform deposition (residual sum 26.6).
analysis.reading_entry: III.1 The Carbon Instability Condition Favors Shallower Heating
analysis.problem: Quiescent cooling models of accreting neutron star crusts suffer from an intrinsic degeneracy where shallow heating overlapping the fuel layer and deep heating beneath it produce nearly identical surface cooling curves by adjusting heating strength $q_a$ and core temperature $T_{\rm c}$, leaving the true physical depth and origin of shallow accretion heating unconstrained.
analysis.method: Thermal evolution is simulated with the dStar code for a neutron star ($M = 1.4\,M_\odot$, $R = 10\text{ km}$, $d = 4.5\text{ kpc}$) under RXTE/ASM reconstructed accretion rate history $\dot{M}(t)$. The model applies local carbon instability criteria $(\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm C}}{\partial T})_P \ge (\frac{\partial\epsilon_{\rm cool}}{\partial T})_P$ with local heating rate $\epsilon_a = \frac{\dot{M}Q_a}{M_a m_u}$, conduction cooling $\epsilon_{\rm cool} = 0.17\frac{K\rho T}{y^2}$, thermal conductivity $K = \frac{\pi^2 c^2 k_{\rm B}^2 T n_e}{3\mu_e \nu_{ei}}$, advective carbon burial/consumption $\frac{dy}{dt}$, and burst energy deposition $e_{\rm b}(y) \propto (y/y_{\rm h})^\beta$ (with $\beta = 0$ or $1/4$), followed by joint spectral fitting across 10 Chandra quiescent epochs ($0.5\text{--}7\text{ keV}$) via Nelder–Mead optimization.
assumptions: The carbon mass fraction in the ignition layer is assumed to be $X_{\rm C} = 0.20$ yielding a nuclear energy release of $\approx 2\times 10^{17}\text{ erg g}^{-1}$.
limits: Conductive cooling models predict superburst decay light curves that remain broader than observed (early flux is underpredicted and late tail is overpredicted by a factor of $\sim 3$ even when accounting for $^{23}{\rm Na}$–$^{23}{\rm Ne}$ Urca shell neutrino losses).

analysis.reason: This paper uses ASKAP POSSUM broadband polarization observations to probe statistical depolarization and Faraday dispersion across the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). It provides valuable empirical constraints on the turbulent magneto-ionic medium and thermal electron density scaling in dwarf irregular galaxies, relevant to intervening sightlines and propagation effects of extragalactic transients.
analysis.result: The fraction of polarized sources is significantly suppressed on-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$) compared to off-SMC ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), accompanied by an enhanced Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 74 \pm 9\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$. Modeling external Faraday dispersion with Burn's law gives $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.32$, implying a tangled random magnetic field strength $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)\,(l_0/0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ ($B_r \approx 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ at the beam scale $\sim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$).
analysis.problem: Determining whether depolarization of background radio sources in the SMC is driven by small-scale thermal electron density fluctuations or turbulent random magnetic fields, and assessing whether small-scale Faraday dispersion matches extrapolations of the large-scale RM power spectrum.
analysis.method: Subtracted SMC diffuse emission, performed RM synthesis and Stokes $QU$-fitting on POSSUM Pilot II data ($800-1088\ \mathrm{MHz}$), and modeled external Faraday dispersion $\sigma_\phi = 0.812\,n_e\,B_\parallel\,\sqrt{l_0\,L} = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ combined with $\mathrm{H}\alpha$-derived emission measure $\left(\frac{\mathrm{EM}}{\mathrm{cm^{-6}\ pc}}\right) \approx 2.75 \left(\frac{I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha,\mathrm{corr}}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \left(\frac{T_e}{10^4\ \mathrm{K}}\right)^{0.942}$.
assumptions: Thermal electron density $n_e$ is assumed to be approximately constant across small scales, attributing Faraday dispersion primarily to random magnetic field fluctuations.
limits: Faraday complexity and multi-component structures are predominantly intrinsic to background sources or foreground Milky Way emission rather than SMC magneto-ionic turbulence.

analysis.reason: The paper uses an unseen-species statistical framework on CHIME/FRB repeaters to demonstrate that repeating FRB sources cease activity within a few years rather than emitting steadily, placing strict demographic constraints on young magnetar engines.
analysis.result: Steady Poisson activity is decisively ruled out ($p < 10^{-4}$, with no mock catalog out of 10,000 yielding $S \le 0.530$). The gap ratio $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred} \approx 1$ at $\Delta \lesssim 60\,\mathrm{d}$ decreases by half within one year. Fitting extinction models yields a characteristic lifetime $\tau = 2.9^{+1.1}_{-0.9}\,\mathrm{yr}$ (single lifetime), an active duration $T_{\rm on} = 800^{+400}_{-400}\,\mathrm{days}$ with duty cycle $d = 0.3^{+0.05}_{-0.2}$ (on/off model), or short-lifetime $\tau_s = 500^{+300}_{-200}\,\mathrm{days}$ with long-lived fraction $\eta = 0.3^{+0.2}_{-0.1}$ (mixture model). The implied birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1 \left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right) \left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right) \left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right) \left(\frac{100\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$, indicating only $\sim 10\%$ of newborn magnetars need to be active repeaters.
analysis.reading_entry: IV The activity is not steady
analysis.problem: Whether repeating FRBs maintain steady Poisson activity over multi-year baselines, and what their true active lifetime is across the source population without being biased by rare hyperactive sources.
analysis.method: Employs Robbins' formula for unseen species estimation, where the burst yield in window $B$ ($T_B$) is predicted from detections $N_{k+1}$ in window $A$ ($T_A$) via $n_k^{\rm pred} = (k+1) N_{k+1} (T_B/T_A)$ independent of rate distribution $f(r)$. Evaluates the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = n^{\rm obs}/n^{\rm pred}$ using sliding windows ($W = 180\,\mathrm{d}$, step $30\,\mathrm{d}$, $k \le 3$), and derives the exposure ratio $t = T_B/T_A$ self-consistently from new source counts via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k\ge 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the discovery and multiwavelength follow-up of WFST0533buha (Bi'an), a fast blue ultraluminous transient (FBUT/LFBOT) candidate that exhibits unusually red blue/NUV colors and rapid photometric evolution, expanding the observational diversity of engine-driven transients.
analysis.result: The transient experienced an ultra-rapid optical rise with $u$-band brightening of $\Delta m_u = 2.45 \pm 0.11\ \mathrm{mag}$ within $\approx 3\ \mathrm{days}$ ($t_{1/2,\mathrm{rise}} = 2.20^{+0.10}_{-0.09}\ \mathrm{days}$, $t_{1/2} < 6\ \mathrm{days}$). At an adopted fiducial redshift $z=0.25$, peak absolute magnitudes reach $M_u = -20.68\ \mathrm{mag}$, $M_g = -20.62\ \mathrm{mag}$, and $M_r = -20.21\ \mathrm{mag}$. Blackbody fitting near peak yields $T_{\rm BB} = (2.07 \pm 0.04) \times 10^4\ \mathrm{K}$, $R_{\rm BB} = (1.12 \pm 0.02) \times 10^{15}\ \mathrm{cm}$, and $L_{\rm BB} = 1.65^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \times 10^{44}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (with $L_{\mathrm{bol}} \sim 5.1 \times 10^{42}\text{--}2.5 \times 10^{44}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ over $0.05 \le z \le 0.30$). VLA detected a faint radio counterpart at $15\ \mathrm{GHz}$ ($22\ \mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$) and $10\ \mathrm{GHz}$ ($19\ \mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$), while Einstein Probe yielded non-detections constraining $0.5\text{--}10\ \mathrm{keV}$ X-ray emission below luminous FBOTs like AT 2020mrf.
analysis.problem: Unveiling the physical mechanism, circumstellar interaction, and radiation physics driving fast blue ultraluminous transients (FBUTs/LFBOTs), whose extreme optical peak luminosities ($M_g \lesssim -20\ \mathrm{mag}$) and rapid half-maximum timescales ($t_{1/2} < 12\ \mathrm{days}$) cannot be powered by standard $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ radioactive decay.

analysis.reason: SN 2025wiu presents an extraordinarily slow light-curve evolution and a rare, prominent post-maximum bump in a Type Ib supernova, offering stringent constraints on shock cooling and circumstellar medium interaction mechanisms.
analysis.result: The optical peak exhibits absolute magnitudes $M_{u}=-17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_{g}=-18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_{r}=-18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, with an early excess consistent with shock-cooling emission from a progenitor of $R_{\star} \sim 4\,R_{\odot}$. A post-maximum bump emerges $\sim 23\,\mathrm{d}$ after maximum, peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with a duration of $\sim 42\,\mathrm{d}$. Arnett's rule yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.47\,M_\odot$ for the main peak, whereas late-time decay indicates $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$, and delayed interaction with circumstellar material of mass $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_{\odot}$ at $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$ (for $\epsilon = 0.5$ and $v_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 8000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) naturally explains the feature.
analysis.reading_entry: VI Bump Properties and Potential Energy Sources
analysis.problem: The light curve of SN 2025wiu exhibits an extraordinary post-maximum bump that deviates markedly from radioactive decay models (${}^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$), and the discrepancy between the Arnett-derived peak nickel mass ($0.47\,M_\odot$) and tail-derived nickel mass ($0.13\,M_\odot$) rules out pure radioactive powering.
analysis.method: Multi-band photometry and optical spectroscopy were acquired with WFST, NOT, and SALT. Early shock cooling was modeled using compact progenitor parameters ($R_\star=4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=2\,M_\odot$, $E=10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$). Light-curve energetics and timescales were modeled using the Arnett analytical relation, the generalized diffusion relation $L_{\mathrm{peak}}=\frac{2}{(\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}})^{2}}\int_{0}^{\beta t_{\mathrm{peak}}}\tau L_{\mathrm{heat}}(\tau)\,d\tau$, gamma-ray deposition $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1-\exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, and diffusion timescale $t_{\mathrm{d}}=\sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}}/(4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}}c)}$.
assumptions: The ejecta opacity remains approximately constant across the analytical framework.
A typical magnetar flare timescale is exceptionally short compared to diffusion ($\Delta t_{\mathrm{flare}}\ll t_{\mathrm{d}}$).
limits: Lack of narrow H/He emission lines at $+110\,\mathrm{d}$ limits visible unshocked dense CSM interaction, requiring hidden or asymmetric geometry.

analysis.reason: This paper presents AttNPE, an interpretable neural posterior estimation framework for fast radio burst cosmology that bypasses expensive likelihood evaluations while explicitly capturing source-level redshift contributions to cosmological and host dispersion measure parameters.
analysis.result: AttNPE infers seven cosmological and astrophysical parameters from 120 localized FRBs, obtaining $\Omega_{\rm m} = 0.3107^{+0.0254}_{-0.0215}$ and constraining the degenerate composite parameter $\mathcal{A} \equiv H_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}$. The posterior matches MCMC benchmarks with Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathrm{JSD} < 0.0043$ and $68\%$ credible interval ratio $r_{68} \in [0.993, 1.095]$. While single-source sensitivity $\Delta\mathrm{NLL}_i$ grows with redshift $z$, intermediate-redshift sources ($0.3 \le z < 0.7$, 40 FRBs) dominate the total attention ($46.2\%$) and posterior response for $\Omega_{\rm m}$ ($44.8\%$), $\Omega_{\rm b}$, and $H_0$ due to the scarcity of high-redshift detections ($z \ge 0.7$, 6 FRBs).
analysis.reading_entry: II.1 FRB dispersion model and conditional likelihood
analysis.problem: Joint Bayesian cosmological inference from localized FRBs requires convolving and marginalizing individual sightline dispersion measure components (Galactic halo $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm halo}$, intergalactic medium $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}$, and host galaxy $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}/(1+z)$), resulting in prohibitive likelihood evaluation costs in standard MCMC analyses.
analysis.method: The framework models extragalactic dispersion as $\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm E},i} = \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm halo},i} + \mathrm{DM}_{{\rm IGM},i} + \frac{\mathrm{DM}_{{\rm host},i}}{1+z_i}$ with mean IGM relation $\langle\mathrm{DM}_{\rm IGM}(z)\rangle = \frac{3cH_0\Omega_{\rm b}f_{\rm d}}{8\pi Gm_p}\int_0^z \frac{\chi_e(z')(1+z')}{E(z')}\,\mathrm{d}z'$. It combines a self-attention catalog embedding with a conditional masked autoregressive flow (MAF) to infer $\bm{\theta} = \{\Omega_{\rm m}, \Omega_{\rm b}, H_0, f_{\rm d}, F, \mu_{\rm host}, \sigma_{\rm host}\}$ trained over $10^6$ forward simulations conditioned on the 120 observed FRB redshifts.
assumptions: All simulated catalogs fix the 120 source redshifts to match the observed catalog, with index $i$ corresponding to redshift $z_i$ throughout.
limits: The sample is limited to 120 localized FRBs meeting $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm E} > 80\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm ISM} \le 0.4\,\mathrm{DM}_{\rm obs}$, with only 6 events at $z \ge 0.7$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first self-consistent 3D radiative transfer simulations that successfully reproduce the early bolometric and multi-band spectral evolution of AT2017gfo, demonstrating that an ad-hoc separate lanthanide-poor component is unnecessary when realistic 3D ejecta geometry and slower post-merger outflow velocity distributions are taken into account.
analysis.result: Scaling ejecta mass to $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving velocities (median velocity $v_r \lesssim 0.09c$) matches the bolometric light curve of AT2017gfo within $\sim 30\%$ at $1.5\text{--}5\,\mathrm{d}$ and reproduces early spectra at $1.4$, $2.4$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$. Velocity compression elevates density by a factor of 8 ($V \propto v_r^3$), increasing $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ and trapping UVOIR radiation so that late ($6\text{--}12\,\mathrm{d}$) luminosity exceeds instantaneous radioactive deposition by $50\%\text{--}80\%$. The photospheric radius scales as $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}} t$ and effective temperature follows $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4} (v_{\mathrm{ph}} t)^{-1/2}$. Distinct transitions are identified: the $\sim 10\,500\,\text{\AA}$ peak is driven by $\mathrm{Sr\;II}\,\lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$; the $\sim 7300\,\text{\AA}$ peak by $\mathrm{Y\;II}\,\lambda 7882$; and the $\sim 13\,500\,\text{\AA}$ shoulder by $\mathrm{La\;III}\,\lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\;III}\,\lambda 14333$. In 3D geometry with $\sim 25\%$ mass in low-lanthanide regions ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$), optical flux at $4500\text{--}5500\,\text{\AA}$ is reproduced without an independent lanthanide-free component. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models mix lanthanides into polar sightlines, reducing $1\,\mathrm{d}$ luminosity threefold and producing an excessively red spectrum. Furthermore, standard expansion opacity overestimates uncollided packet transmission $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}} \approx e^{-1} \approx 0.37$ for optically thick lines ($\tau_l \gg 1$), overestimating early spectral flux by $10\%\text{--}20\%$.
analysis.problem: Previous 3D dynamical ejecta models possessed insufficient mass ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and excessively high velocities relative to empirical inferences for AT2017gfo ($M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), leaving unresolved whether early blue and optical emissions require an independent, distinct lanthanide-poor ejecta component and whether common 2D azimuthal averaging and expansion opacity approximations distort inferred physical properties.
analysis.method: Simulations utilize the 3D time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS with homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$) mapped from a $2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ SPH binary neutron star merger snapshot at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Nuclear heating solves the Bateman equations for $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $^{254}\mathrm{Cf}$ fission, tracking non-instantaneous density-dependent charged particle thermalization and $\gamma$-ray transport. Ionization and excitation are treated in LTE via Saha-Boltzmann equations at local electron temperature $T_e$. Calculations employ the AD3 dataset containing $\approx 4.9 \times 10^7$ bound-bound transitions across 323 ions of 83 elements with wavelength-calibrated lanthanide levels. Radiative transfer benchmarks line-by-line (LBL) macroatom treatments against capped line-binned opacities with optical depth $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and expansion opacities $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i (1 - e^{-\tau_i})$.
assumptions: Homologous expansion ($r = v_r t$, $V \propto v_r^3$) from $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$ onward.
limits: Velocity compression is an ad-hoc phenomenological scaling to mimic slower post-merger disk outflows rather than a self-consistent hydrodynamic simulation.

analysis.reason: This paper presents detailed NICER timing and time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the brightest thermonuclear burst in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658, providing critical observational constraints on burst-disc interaction and accretion physics in compact objects.
analysis.result: Using simultaneous reflection and persistent emission scaling (Model C), the burst peak exhibits an increased persistent scaling factor $f_{a,1}=59.6\pm 0.6$ and sub-unity reflection fractions $f_{r,1}=0.82\pm 0.15$ and $f_{r,2}=0.55\pm 0.06$. The direct burst bolometric luminosity peaks at $L_{\rm bol} \approx 0.68\,L_{\rm Edd}$, below the Eddington limit despite PRE characteristics. In the burst tail ($>200\,\mathrm{s}$), the absorption column density increases by $\approx 34\%$ ($N_{\mathrm{H}} = (2.42^{+0.13}_{-0.10})\times 10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) and the accretion disc temperature increases by $\approx 15\%$ ($kT_{\mathrm{disc}} = 0.78^{+0.04}_{-0.03}\,\mathrm{keV}$), confirming burst-induced disc heating and geometric puffing.

analysis.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the soft X-ray excess ($<1.5\,\mathrm{keV}$) during super-bright thermonuclear bursts, the thermodynamic and structural impact of burst irradiation on the accretion disc, and whether persistent accretion emission evolves during the burst.

analysis.reason: This paper develops a Bayesian framework combining FRB dispersion measures and mock galaxy surveys in IllustrisTNG to deconstruct the cosmic baryon distribution across cosmic web environments, directly relevant to FRB propagation and baryon census studies.
analysis.result: The reconstruction accurately recovers the cosmic ionized baryon density as $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (consistent with the IllustrisTNG true value of $0.0462$ at the $0.2\sigma$ level), corresponding to $\Omega_{\mathrm{b}} = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{\mathrm{ion}} = 0.95$. Approximately $75\%$ of free electrons reside in diffuse low-density environments ($\rho_{\mathrm{m}}/\rho_{\mathrm{crit}} \le 2.94$). Inferred gas mass fractions across structures are $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{void}} = 0.186 \pm 0.012$, $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{filament}} = 0.179 \pm 0.015$, and $f_{\mathrm{gas}}^{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.046 \pm 0.014$ (against true values $0.167$, $0.173$, and $0.067$), recovering $98.60\%$ of global ionized baryons ($\langle r_{\mathrm{FRB}} \rangle_M = 0.986\,r_{\mathrm{theo}}$).
analysis.problem: Cosmological dispersion measure $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{LSS}}(\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}, z) = \frac{3cH_0\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}}{8\pi G m_{\mathrm{p}}} f_{\mathrm{ion}} f_{\mathrm{e}} \int_0^z \frac{1+z'}{E(z')} [1+\delta_{\mathrm{e}}(\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}, z')]\,\mathrm{d}z'$ is an integrated line-of-sight quantity that cannot directly resolve the local spatial density contrast $\delta_{\mathrm{e}}$ and electron distribution across distinct cosmic web environments (voids, filaments, and halos).
analysis.method: Using IllustrisTNG TNG300-1 simulations ($z \in [0, 1.5]$), large-scale structure is partitioned into $M=8$ logarithmic matter density bins. A discrete linear forward system $\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{r} + \mathbf{n}$ relates line-of-sight DM to electron-to-matter density ratios $r_i = n_{\mathrm{e}, i}/\rho_i$, with theoretical expectation $r_{\mathrm{theo}} = \frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{b}}}{\Omega_{\mathrm{m}}\mu_{\mathrm{e}}m_{\mathrm{p}}} f_{\mathrm{ion}} \approx (7.84 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$. A 4-parameter profile $\mathbf{r}(\theta)$ parameterized by $\theta = \{\mathcal{S}, \log\rho_{\mathrm{tran}}, w_{\rho}, \alpha_{\rho}\}$ is sampled via MCMC (`emcee`) across $N=470$ quasi-independent lines of sight ($|R_{ij}| < 0.3$). Visible matter density from a simulated Euclid-like galaxy survey $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{gal}} = \bar{\rho}_{\mathrm{m}}[1 + \delta_{\mathrm{gal}}/b]$ is combined to reconstruct $\hat{n}_{\mathrm{e}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{FRB}} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{gal}}$.
assumptions: AGN and supernova feedback drive hot gas outward from central halos into outskirts, suppressing the electron-to-matter density ratio $r(\theta)$ in high-density regions relative to $r_{\mathrm{theo}}$.
limits: Severe spectroscopic incompleteness (e.g. 80% galaxy subsampling) reduces density reconstruction accuracy by 27%–31% in low-density bins and 46%–53% in high-density bins, and redshift-space distortions (RSD) introduce interpolation biases along the line of sight.
